title: The universal fixed-point functor is a closed subscheme
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be a separated finite-type $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $b:G\times_kY\to Y$ be an action: after every base change $b(1,y)=y$ and $b(g,b(g',y))=b(gg',y)$, with products as in [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every commutative $k$-algebra $B$, put
$$\mathrm{Fix}_b(B)=\{y\in Y(B): b_{B'}(g,y_{B'})=y_{B'}\text{ for every commutative }B\text{-algebra }B'\text{ and }g\in G(B')\}.$$
Here $Y(B)$ means $k$-morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. This subfunctor is represented by a closed subscheme $Y^G\hookrightarrow Y$: the inclusion identifies $Y^G(B)$ with $\mathrm{Fix}_b(B)$ for every $B$. The restricted action $G\times_kY^G\to Y$ equals the projection followed by $Y^G\hookrightarrow Y$. For every $k$-scheme $W$ and morphism $u:W\to Y$, $u$ factors through $Y^G$ if and only if $b\circ(\mathrm{id}_G\times u)=u\circ p_W$ as morphisms $G\times_kW\to Y$. No smoothness or reducedness of $G$, $Y$, $B$, or $W$ is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 7.1 and proof, printed pp.138–139, together with its preceding largest-fixed-closed-subscheme formulation. The final factorization clause is its representing property, tested on affine charts of W. This theorem in the stated generality has no Stacks tag.

proof.text: Put $X=Y\times_kY$ and $d=\Delta_Y:Y\hookrightarrow X$, closed by the separatedness hypothesis. The scheme $X$ is finite type: its second projection is a base change of $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and its structure morphism is the composite with $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, so both assertions of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] apply. It is also separated. Indeed, after rearranging the four factors using [def-pc-fibre-product], its diagonal is $\Delta_Y\times_k\Delta_Y$. Factor this map by first applying $\Delta_Y$ to the first factor and then to the second. Each factor is a base change of $d$, hence closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Their composite is closed directly from [def-weil-closed-immersion]: over an affine target the successive closed subschemes are $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}((A/I)/J)$, the latter being a quotient of $A$ by the inverse image of $J$. Thus the affine quotient criterion proves the composite closed (the elementary argument of Stacks Tag 01QS, label morphisms-lemma-composition-closed-immersion). This verifies all target-scheme hypotheses of the factorization-locus lemma without assuming $Y$ affine.

source.place: Theorem 7.1, pp.138–139, diagonal construction; finite-type closure as Stacks 01T3/01T4; elementary closed-composite argument as Stacks 01QS.

proof.text: Let $F=(b,p_Y):G\times_kY\to X$, defined by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Apply [lem-sfb-constant-source-closed-factorization-locus] with constant source $G$, parameter scheme $Y$, target $X$, closed subscheme $d:Y\hookrightarrow X$, and family $F$. The hypotheses on $G$ and $Y$ are exactly the assumptions of the item, and Step 1 checked $X$. Obtain a closed immersion $l:L\hookrightarrow Y$ such that, for every $k$-scheme $W$ and $u:W\to Y$, $u$ factors through $L$ exactly when $(b\circ(\mathrm{id}_G\times u),u\circ p_W)$ factors through $d$. By the product universal property, a pair $(a,c)$ factors through the diagonal precisely when $a=c$: the lift must be $a=c$, and conversely $d\circ a=(a,a)$. Therefore $u$ factors through $L$ if and only if $b\circ(\mathrm{id}_G\times u)=u\circ p_W$.

source.place: Theorem 7.1, pp.138–139, Cartesian diagram; 1.76–1.78 and their proofs 1.100–1.105, pp.36–38, expressed by the existing constant-source factorization lemma.

proof.text: Fix a commutative $k$-algebra $B$ and $y:\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y$. Write $a=b\circ(\mathrm{id}_G\times y)$ and $c=y\circ p_B$ on $G_B=G\times_k\operatorname{Spec}B$. If $a=c$, precomposing with the map $(g,\operatorname{Spec}(B'\leftarrow B)):\operatorname{Spec}B'\to G_B$ of [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $b_{B'}(g,y_{B'})=y_{B'}$ for every $B$-algebra $B'$ and $g\in G(B')$. Conversely, suppose all these equalities hold. Cover $G_B$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The projection $V\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ makes $R$ a $B$-algebra by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and the other projection gives $g\in G(R)$. The map $(g,V\to\operatorname{Spec}B)$ is the inclusion $V\hookrightarrow G_B$, by its two projections. The assumed equality for $B'=R$ says exactly $a|_V=c|_V$. Hence $a=c$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. This uses every affine chart, rather than just geometric points, and applies with nilpotents in $B$ or $R$.

source.place: Theorem 7.1, p.138, all R-algebras R prime in the definition; affine-chart expansion of the equality of the two natural maps, p.139. Stacks 01IT and 00AN justify the affine test.

proof.text: Set $Y^G=L$. By [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed], $l$ is a monomorphism, so composition with $l$ injects $L(B)$ into $Y(B)$. Steps 2 and 3 identify its image with $\mathrm{Fix}_b(B)$. These identifications are natural in $B$, since both maps to $Y(B)$ are composition with $l$ and scalar extension is precomposition with the induced spectrum map. Finally take $W=L$ and $u=l$ in Step 2: $l$ factors through itself by the identity, so $b\circ(\mathrm{id}_G\times l)=l\circ p_L$. This is the restricted-action assertion. Step 2 already proves the required equivalence for every scheme $W$, with no finiteness, smoothness, or reducedness assumption on $W$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N6-d5e61d321 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Milne iAG2017 Theorem 7.1 and its proof on printed pp.138–139. The item's Fix_b functor and its separatedness hypotheses match the source. Statement and stmt_deps are unchanged and there are no new nodes. Step 1: X=Y×Y is finite type by clauses (1) and (2) of lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change. It is separated because its diagonal is Δ_Y×Δ_Y, built from base changes of Δ_Y (closed by lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change). That composites of closed immersions are closed is argued correctly in two lines from the affine criterion in def-weil-closed-immersion; the step names Stacks 01QS without a node. lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products states this fact, but it is a split node of unit sk-thm-br, so citing it would be a cross-unit tool use; the inline argument is acceptable. Step 2 applies lem-sfb-constant-source-closed-factorization-locus (same unit, no cycle) with constant source G, parameter Y, target X, closed immersion Δ_Y and family (b,p_Y). All hypotheses hold, and f∘(id×u)=(b∘(id×u),u∘p_W) factors through Δ exactly when the two maps are equal. The lemma quantifies over all k-schemes T, so the arbitrary-W clause is exact. Step 3 shows equality on G_B is equivalent to the Fix_b condition via affine charts Spec R of G_B (basis and gluing nodes): the chart inclusion is (g,V→Spec B), and no affine intersections or geometric points are assumed. Step 4 gets monicity from lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed, identifies the image, gets naturality, and takes W=L for the restricted action; marking it elementary is justified. Small cases: trivial action; Y empty; G_m scaling on A^1; μ_p scaling in characteristic p, where the universal 1+t forces x=0; α_p translation gives the empty scheme; B=0. No duplicate: the torus and μ_n fixed-scheme nodes assume representability or concern special groups. No SGA citation, no fixes and no tool_uses.

lean.statement: theorem exists_universal_fixed_subscheme {k : Type u} [Field k] (G Y : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] [IsSeparated G.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] [IsSeparated Y.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom] [ModObj G Y] : ∃ (F : Over (Spec (.of k))) (i : F ⟶ Y), IsClosedImmersion i.left ∧ (∀ (A : CommAlgCat.{u} k) (y : (algSpec (.of k)).obj (op A) ⟶ Y), (∃! z : (algSpec (.of k)).obj (op A) ⟶ F, z ≫ i = y) ↔ ∀ (A' : CommAlgCat.{u} k) (f : A ⟶ A') (g : (algSpec (.of k)).obj (op A') ⟶ G), g • ((algSpec (.of k)).map f.op ≫ y) = (algSpec (.of k)).map f.op ≫ y) ∧ (G ◁ i) ≫ ModObj.smul (M := G) (X := Y) = snd G F ≫ i ∧ ∀ (W : Over (Spec (.of k))) (v : W ⟶ Y), (∃ w : W ⟶ F, w ≫ i = v) ↔ (G ◁ v) ≫ ModObj.smul (M := G) (X := Y) = snd G W ≫ v
